title: Sparse and weak-measurement certification of graph-edge entanglement in PXP scar wavepackets
authors: Ximo Wang, Yichi Zhang, Qiwei Han, Xi Zhao, Yuhang Wang, Chunxiao Du, Rui Li, Wenxiu Li, Hao Zhang
abstract: An imperfect many-body revival does not by itself certify the entanglement of the returning state. We give a finite-record protocol for graph-edge localizable entanglement along scar wavepackets of a graph-dressed PXP chain. The target cluster state has nonzero energy variance, so neither an exact target eigenstate nor a dark-state embedding is assumed. Fresh binary probes of the undeformed Hamiltonians Pauli terms have a fully separable explanation, even within the dressed blockade sector. Adding local graph-stabilizer probes makes established entanglement witnesses accessible with simultaneous confidence bounds. For a specified square-root instrument, an imposed worst-case disturbance budget fixes the strength that minimizes the equal-allocation Hoeffding sufficient sampling cost. A local commutator bound accounts for finite-duration ancilla pulses while the Hamiltonian remains active. We test the protocol on chains through twenty spins, under perturbed dynamics, and with independent implementations. At the first twenty-spin return, synthetic weak records certify all nineteen graph edges. Generator, two-color, bounded-weight, and full-group benchmarks separate this localizable resource from genuine multipartite certification. The protocol measures recoverable entanglement in a known scar wavepacket, with explicit calibration and limits on its physical and statistical interpretation.
summary: This work introduces a novel, resource-efficient protocol to certify graph-edge entanglement in a quantum chain undergoing complex dynamics. By using weak measurements and local stabilizer probes, the authors overcome limitations associated with assuming perfect measurements or pure target states. The protocol provides a quantifiable measure of recoverable entanglement under realistic noise and disturbance constraints.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to certify graph-edge entanglement in a quantum many-body system using only sparse, weak measurement records obtained during evolution.
main_result: A finite-record protocol was developed that successfully certifies all graph edges in a test chain up to twenty spins, distinguishing this local resource from genuine multipartite entanglement.
method: The method employs local graph-stabilizer probes within a weak measurement framework, utilizing Hoeffding's inequality to establish simultaneous confidence bounds on the measured entanglement witnesses.
model_or_system: The system is a graph-dressed PXP chain, a quantum many-body model whose target state is explicitly non-eigenstate and has a non-zero energy variance.
key_observables: Graph-edge negativity, generator fidelity ($F_G$), and local Pauli expectation values ($a_i$).
important_parameters: Measurement strength ($\mu$), worst-case disturbance budget ($\delta$), and the number of spins ($N$).
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes a worst-case disturbance budget and accounts for finite-duration ancilla pulses, explicitly avoiding assumptions about the target state being an exact eigenstate.
figures_summary: The notes reference testing the protocol on chains up to twenty spins, showing that the first twenty-spin return certifies all nineteen graph edges.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of weak measurement certification, details the mathematical framework using weak probes and confidence bounds, derives the local certificate based on negativity, and validates the protocol through simulations on the PXP chain.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, resource-aware method for quantifying entanglement in complex, non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, which is crucial for understanding quantum computation feasibility in realistic noisy environments.
